alerts.title: Assam floods: over 100 dead, recovery underway but rivers still elevated in Upper Assam
alerts.summary: Weeks of catastrophic monsoon flooding across Upper Assam — worst in Sivasagar, Nazira, Charaideo and Jorhat districts — killed over 100 people and displaced roughly 700,000. Many residents have begun returning home as floodwaters recede and 52 relief camps continue operating, but around 119,000 hectares of cropland remain submerged and rehabilitation is still underway across affected districts.
alerts.impact: Serviceability recovering but fragile — Upper Assam (Sivasagar/Nazira/Charaideo/Jorhat): keep a light NS watch on flood-hit pincodes as roads and bridges are still being repaired; resume normal manifestation gradually and coordinate with Delhivery/Xpressbees on NE routing around Guwahati hub as access improves.

alerts.title: Assam: fresh Brahmaputra riverbank erosion at Tingkhong's Mohanaghat in Dibrugarh, CM engages IIT-Guwahati
alerts.summary: Fresh riverbank erosion by the Brahmaputra has hit the Mohanaghat area near Tingkhong Bhoga Ali in Dibrugarh district, the latest in a string of erosion incidents this monsoon across Chabua, Balijan, Pukhurijan, Dinjan and Rahmoria that Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma toured on August 2. The state government has now engaged IIT-Guwahati to design a long-term erosion-control solution for the Brahmaputra basin.
alerts.impact: Watch list — Dibrugarh belt (Tingkhong, Chabua, Dinjan, Rahmoria): flag riverside pincodes as erosion-risk, expect gradual land loss to keep some approach roads unstable through the monsoon; no full stoppage yet but build in extra transit time for last-mile in these panchayats.

alerts.title: Himachal Pradesh: Kiratpur-Manali highway hit by repeated landslides/shooting stones, 118 roads shut statewide
alerts.summary: The Pandoh stretch of the Kiratpur-Manali National Highway (Mandi-Kullu) has been restored to one-way traffic after its latest landslide closure, but the corridor keeps getting hit — most recently by shooting stones near Mehla village in Bilaspur district, which forced police to suspend all vehicle movement beyond Mandi Bharari Chowk and divert traffic via Nauni Chowk/NH-205 towards Swarghat. Statewide, 118 roads remain blocked by monsoon damage, 44 of them in Mandi district alone.
alerts.impact: Critical serviceability risk — Mandi/Kullu/Manali/Bilaspur corridor: continue holding non-time-critical linehaul on this NH, use the Nauni Chowk-NH205-Swarghat diversion where police permit, and keep 3-5 day buffer stock at Mandi/Kullu hubs given the highway has now closed and reopened multiple times this month.

alerts.title: Manipur: NH202 Imphal-Ukhrul road still in deplorable condition, Kamjong bailey bridge unrepaired since July
alerts.summary: The August flash floods and landslides across Senapati, Ukhrul and Kamjong hill districts washed away roads, farmland and bridges, and NH202 (Imphal-Ukhrul road) remains in deplorable, monsoon-battered condition with persistent roadblocks stranding vehicles. The Bailey bridge over the Namban/Nambalok river in Kamjong district — the only link for Chatric and 12 neighbouring border villages — has still not been repaired since it was destroyed in July.
alerts.impact: Serviceability loss — Ukhrul/Kamjong/Senapati pincodes: keep border villages served via the Kamjong bridge flagged non-serviceable, route Imphal-hub linehaul with extra transit buffer on NH202, and monitor for continued non-adherence in this hill-district LM belt through the monsoon.

alerts.title: Meghalaya: Shillong-Dawki road's Laitlyngkot stretch reopens with night-travel restrictions, landslide risk continues
alerts.summary: The Laitlyngkot-Lyngkyrdem stretch of the Shillong-Dawki Road (NH-206) — closed for weeks after landslides — reopened to all vehicular traffic from August 10 following a joint safety inspection. Night-time movement restrictions remain in force, and with the monsoon still active authorities continue to warn of landslide, rockfall and road-instability risk, advising against non-essential travel during and right after heavy rain.
alerts.impact: Watch list — East Khasi Hills/Dawki corridor: daytime LM/FM movement can resume on this stretch, but keep night dispatches suspended and hold a contingency buffer given this road has closed repeatedly (April, June, August) this monsoon season.

alerts.title: Sikkim: recurring landslides at NH-10's 20th Mile cut Singtam-Rangpo link, West Sikkim's Gyalshing-Legship route also blocked
alerts.summary: Expanding land instability at the 20th Mile point on NH-10's Singtam-Rangpo stretch (near ATTC College and the Singtam tunnel portal) has repeatedly blocked this key East Sikkim link through the month; clearance crews are working the site but officials warn restoration will take time. Separately, the Gyalshing-Legship route in West Sikkim has also been cut off by landslides. NHIDCL has proposed four tunnels on the Rangpo-Singtam stretch as a long-term fix.
alerts.impact: Serviceability loss risk — East Sikkim (Singtam-Rangpo) and West Sikkim (Gyalshing-Legship): route Siliguri-Gangtok linehaul via the Singtam-Duga-Rangpo diversion, flag West Sikkim pincodes served via Gyalshing-Legship as at-risk, and pre-position extra buffer stock at the Siliguri gateway hub.

alerts.title: Gujarat: red alert for 13 districts as extreme rainfall batters Surat, Kheda and Anand
alerts.summary: IMD issued a red alert for very heavy rainfall across 13 Gujarat districts as central and south Gujarat were battered by extreme rain on August 26, with Surat, Kheda and Anand the hardest-hit; parts of Saurashtra/Kutch also saw rainfall thousands of percent above normal for the date, driven by a land-based deep depression pulling moisture from both the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea.
alerts.impact: Serviceability risk — Surat/Kheda/Anand belt: flag flood-prone pincodes non-serviceable while the red alert holds, pre-position buffer stock at the Ahmedabad/Vadodara hubs, and coordinate with Delhivery/Shadowfax on alternate routing around waterlogged stretches in these three districts.

alerts.title: Kerala: orange alert for Idukki, Wayanad, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Kannur as heavy rain continues to Aug 29
alerts.summary: IMD has placed Idukki, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad and Kannur on orange alert for August 28, extending to Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Palakkad, Malappuram and Wayanad on August 29, forecasting extremely heavy rain of around 20cm along with squally winds up to 50-60kmph off the Arabian Sea coast. All other districts remain on yellow alert.
alerts.impact: Watch list — Idukki/Wayanad/Malappuram/Kottayam hill and highland pincodes: pre-build 2-3 day buffer stock, monitor for fresh landslide-triggered village cutoffs given this belt's monsoon history, and be ready to flag NS for hill-taluka pincodes if the alert is upgraded.

alerts.title: Fresh Bay of Bengal low-pressure system to form near West Bengal-North Odisha coast around Aug 29
alerts.summary: A cyclonic circulation is already active over the northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining West Bengal-North Odisha coast, and IMD expects it to consolidate into a fresh low-pressure area around August 29 — the latest in a run of back-to-back systems that have already brought repeated heavy rain to the region this month. Squally winds and rough seas are expected off the West Bengal-Odisha coast.
alerts.impact: Cost/route watch — Balasore/Bhadrak/coastal Odisha and South Bengal hubs: pre-position buffer stock ahead of the system's landfall window, advise fishermen-adjacent coastal pincodes may see short LM slowdowns, and monitor for a repeat of the river-flooding pattern seen earlier this month in Balasore's Basta block.

alerts.title: Petrol/diesel hold at multi-city highs; commercial LPG down for 2nd straight month, CNG/PNG unchanged
alerts.summary: Retail petrol and diesel prices remain unchanged since OMCs' May 25 hike — Delhi ₹102.12/₹95.20, Mumbai ₹111.21/₹97.83, Hyderabad ₹115.69/₹103.82 (petrol/diesel per litre). Commercial 19kg LPG cylinders were cut by ₹202-209 in major metros on August 1 — the second straight monthly cut — while domestic 14.2kg LPG has stayed at ₹941.50 since June and CNG/PNG rates are unchanged in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad despite crude prices rising ~24% last month on US-Iran tensions.
alerts.impact: Cost watch, no action yet: no immediate LM/FM disruption. Track weekly for early signal on Delhivery/Shadowfax/Xpressbees fuel-surcharge asks — sustained high crude with flat retail fuel prices keeps margin pressure building ahead of the next OMC pricing cycle.
